page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor, built on the x86_64 architecture and operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The instance provisions 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with exactly 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. Accelerated hardware features such as GPUs are absent on this instance model.

Storage and network configurations are tailored toward distributed and networked environments. The instance does not include local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external cloud storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent file storage. Network capability is supported by a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the instance, requiring explicit networking configuration for external Internet routing.

The high vCPU allocation combined with a moderate memory density delivers cost efficiency for compute-bound operations that do not require massive per-core memory capacities. This architectural trade-off reduces memory overhead costs while maximizing processing parallelization. Appropriate workloads for the ecs.c6a.32xlarge include large-scale batch processing, scientific simulations, video transcoding, distributed compilation pipelines, and compute-heavy web application tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It provides 128 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage volumes for data persistence. Network traffic is accommodated via a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted. By maintaining a lean memory profile relative to its high core count, the server prioritizes parallel compute throughput over large memory footprints. This structural trade-off renders the instance well positioned for compute-heavy, parallelized workloads including scientific computation, continuous integration and build clusters, batch processing, and high-throughput application servers.
